headline: High: pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API defaults create leakage and cascading-error risk when paired with a non-runnable docs-only NLP list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp has no runnable I/O surfaces or shared channel, so it cannot directly inject into pipecat by default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or an external wrapper, while pipecat’s shared bus could amplify malformed text if introduced. This is a weak, indirect pathway, not a default one.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies awesome-nlp content into pipecat prompts or bus messages
IF a wrapper forwards untrusted text from awesome-nlp into pipecat without sanitization
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and prompts
Add a provenance tag to any bridged text
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions
requires-engineering: add content filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp is docs-only and shows no data handling, but pipecat touches text, conversation state, and can call many third-party APIs by default. If both are run in a shared workspace or bus, pipecat can ingest and transmit copied content beyond the local environment. The pairwise leakage path is plausible even though awesome-nlp itself is not a runtime agent.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem, clipboard, or bus carrying user text
IF pipecat is configured to send conversation content to any listed external API
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Turn off external API providers in pipecat
Redact sensitive text before handoff
Use local-only inference endpoints
requires-engineering: enforce per-message data-class allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or network permissions and is not runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. pipecat supports shared-bus multi-instance operation, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable state in the profiles. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory or bus
IF pipecat instances are configured to mutate shared state outside the documented shared bus
mitigations: Keep pipecat instances isolated per session
Avoid shared writable directories
Use file locks in the orchestrator
Restrict pipecat to read-only inputs
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a curated NLP list, so its outputs are likely treated as authoritative references; pipecat can consume text and route it into downstream speech/LLM services. If the list is used as source material without verification, errors or stale links can cascade into generated responses or actions. The pathway is plausible, but not directly evidenced as default automation.
conditions: IF pipecat uses awesome-nlp entries as source facts or prompts
IF downstream services act on pipecat output without human verification
mitigations: Verify source entries before use
Add a human review step for sourced facts
Limit pipecat to summarization, not action-taking
Log provenance for every imported fact
requires-engineering: add citation validation before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class or residency mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, and pipecat’s profile does not specify regulated data handling or a residency boundary. The only concrete compliance concern is that pipecat can route text/audio to third-party APIs, but without a stated regulated data class this remains a limited, policy-dependent risk. The other agent is not cited because it has no touched data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through pipecat to any external provider
IF the operator relies on pipecat defaults without a retention or DPA review
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external APIs
Review provider DPAs and retention settings
Disable analytics and telemetry
Use local-only providers for sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
